questions.q: What does tool calling let a model do?
options: Run Java code directly inside the model
Ask your application to call a Java method and use the result
questions.why: The model only requests a call; Spring AI executes your method and sends the result back.

questions.q: Which annotation turns a Java method into a tool?
Why does the tool description matter so much?
options: It is shown to end users
The model uses it to decide when and how to call the tool
questions.why: Clear names and descriptions are how the model picks the right tool.

questions.q: How do you give tools to a single request?
questions.why: .tools(...) per request, or .defaultTools(...) on the builder; per-request tools are added to the defaults.

questions.q: Your Ollama model returns an error that it does not support tools. Why?
options: Not every model is trained for tool calling: pick one with the 'tools' capability
questions.why: In this course, gemma3:4b has no tool capability, so we switched to qwen2.5:3b.

quizzes.title: The tool loop as an advisor

questions.q: In Spring AI 2.0, what drives the tool calling loop?
options: The ChatModel implementation of each provider
The auto-registered ToolCallingAdvisor in the advisor chain
questions.why: The loop became a composable advisor in 2.0.

questions.q: One question needed findOrder, then daysUntil. How many model calls happened?
questions.why: Call 1 asks for findOrder, call 2 asks for daysUntil, call 3 writes the final answer.

questions.q: Your advisor has order ToolCallingAdvisor.DEFAULT_ORDER + 100. Where does it run?
options: Inside the loop: once per model call
questions.why: Advisors ordered after the tool advisor sit inside the loop and see every iteration.

questions.q: What does ToolSearchToolCallingAdvisor do?
options: Sends only a search tool first, then the tools the model discovers: fewer tokens with many tools
questions.why: Progressive tool disclosure, useful with dozens or hundreds of tools.

questions.q: In the lab, tool search with qwen2.5:3b failed. What did we learn?
options: Progressive disclosure needs a capable model; with 10 tools, sending them all is fine
questions.why: It cut prompt tokens, but small models did not use the search tool reliably.

questions.q: What is the difference between a workflow and an agent?
options: A workflow follows code paths you define; an agent lets the model direct its own steps and tools
questions.why: Workflows are more predictable, which suits most business tasks.

questions.q: Which pattern classifies an input, then sends it to a specialised prompt?
questions.why: Routing: classify with structured output, then pick the expert.

questions.q: Which pattern drafts, reviews, and retries with feedback?
questions.why: A generator and an evaluator in a loop, with a maximum number of attempts.

questions.q: Why check the word count in Java instead of asking the reviewer model?
options: Models are unreliable at counting; code checks what code can check
It is required by Spring AI
questions.why: In the lab, the drafter wrote 'Approximately 85 words' under a much longer reply.

questions.q: The reviewer approved a reply claiming a refund that never happened. Best fix?
options: Add deterministic checks or human approval for risky actions, and real tools for real actions
questions.why: LLM judges miss things; risky outputs need guardrails.

questions.q: Who executes the Java method when a model 'calls a tool'?
Which annotation documents a tool parameter for the model?
A tool must count days until a delivery date. Why compute it in the tool, not in the model?
options: Models are reliable at date math
Date math is deterministic code; models can get it wrong

questions.q: Tools on the builder are .defaultTools(a). The request adds .tools(b). Which tools are available?
Every iteration of the tool loop resends all tool definitions. What is the consequence?
Which property disables the automatic tool loop for the whole app?
Tool search failed with 'context must contain a non-null value for chat_memory_conversation_id'. Fix?
options: Add ChatMemory.CONVERSATION_ID as an advisor param

questions.q: Your app has 300 tools. Which approach scales best with a capable model?
options: ToolSearchToolCallingAdvisor with a Lucene or vector index

questions.q: Which pattern runs independent subtasks at the same time and combines the results?
What must every evaluator-optimizer loop have?
How did the lab use a stronger model only for reviewing?

challenge.title: Travel planner agent
challenge.task: Build GET /plan?city=...&days=... that plans a short trip with 3 tools: getWeather(city, date), findHotels(city, maxPrice) and getEvents(city, date). Return a TripPlan record (days, hotel, activities, totalCost).
requirements: Implement the 3 tools with @Tool/@ToolParam over fake in-memory data, and compute totalCost in Java
Log every iteration of the tool loop with an advisor placed inside the loop
Route requests: 'budget' trips use a cheaper prompt, 'luxury' trips another
Add an evaluator-optimizer step (max 3 drafts) that rejects plans exceeding the budget, checked in code
Use a tool-capable model (e.g. qwen2.5:3b) and write down how many model calls one plan takes
selfCheck: The plan never contains a hotel above maxPrice
totalCost is always computed in Java, never by the model
You can explain each line of your loop log
